claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is single-phase BCC and dendritic.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Partially substituting Ta with Ti will improve yield-strength retention at 1273 K.
Mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering are suitable synthesis routes for the proposed Ti-for-Ta substitution.
Increasing the Ti-to-Ta ratio will modify lattice distortion through changes in atomic-size distribution and solid-solution effects.
Increasing the Ti-to-Ta ratio may change grain-boundary characteristics.
Increasing Ti relative to Ta will enhance lattice strain and solid-solution strengthening.
The proposed compositional change will raise the activation energy for dislocation motion.
The proposed compositional change will slow diffusional softening at high temperature.
The modified alloy will achieve more than approximately a 15–20% increase in yield strength over 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The modified alloy will maintain compressive-strength performance similar to the baseline.
The proposed alloy is applicable as an intermediate bonding layer between W and CuCrZr under thermal gradients reaching at least 1273 K.

contradictions.description: The prediction calls for compressive strength to remain similar to baseline, whereas the falsification rule can be read as requiring a 15–20% improvement in compressive strength as well as yield strength. Under that reading, the predicted similar compressive performance would itself trigger falsification.
